hypotheses.prediction: recall@300 >= 0.90 over the held-out recessive diseases, degraded Zemojtel-style (1-2 terms blurred to a parent, 1-2 noise terms), with a bootstrap interval reported beside it.
hypotheses.reasoning: Measured, not argued: recall@300 is 0.360 against a predicted 0.90, and the interval excludes it by a wide margin. The plan's remedy — raise N until 0.90 is met — does not apply: recall@1000 is only 0.565 and a quarter of held-out genes are unrankable at any N, so no cutoff of a phenotype-only ranker reaches 0.90 on this corpus. Step 2 must therefore not treat the target set as high-recall coverage; the genome-wide route of step 4 becomes the safety net it was designed to be.
hypotheses.refuted_by: recall@300 < 0.90. N is then raised until it is met, before step 2's bait is built, and the raise is recorded.
hypotheses.statement: Held-out recall@300 of the phenotype-only ranker is at least 0.90 on the recessive-disease benchmark, so a target set of the top 300 genes is large enough to be worth baiting.

hands_to.what: The 404-row tiered target set and the 396-row decoy set become step 2's bait design (core ±50kb, net ±2kb padding) and its statistical null (H020 asks whether decoys yield fewer biallelic candidates than targets). Step 2 also inherits the load-bearing caveat verbatim: a gene absent from this set is not excluded, only unbaited — which is why step 4 exists as a genome-wide check that never consults this list.

inherits.what: Nothing from a prior iteration-2 step — this is the entry point of the blind re-derivation. It reads only the clinical HPO terms and public reference data (the HPO ontology release, the curation corpus, Ensembl gene models); no genomic file of this child other than the public reference gene model is touched, which is what keeps the blind gate green.

narrative.summary: Iteration 2 re-derives the case blind: no iteration-1 table, candidate gene or rank was read to build this step, and the gate that checks that (`mva-science check --blind`) is enforced by tooling, not by promise. Step 1 ranks every HPO-curated gene against the proband's 7 clinical terms (plus an 8th, parental-history term) with two independent rankers, and turns the top 300 plus a mechanism-term carve-out into a 404-gene target set with a 396-gene shape-matched decoy set alongside it as a null. Four claims were pre-registered and all four are resolved: only H013 (a recessive chromosome-instability gene is in the set) held. Held-out recall@300 was measured twice — once on a 200-disease sample (0.360) and once, after entry 091 removed the sampling, on the full population of 3,240 eligible diseases (0.335, tighter interval) — and both land far under the 0.90 the step needed to call this set complete coverage.
narrative.verdict: H012 (recall@300 ≥ 0.90) is refuted: 0.360 [0.295, 0.420] on 200 diseases, confirmed at 0.335 [0.318, 0.350] on the full 3,240-disease population in entry 091 — slightly worse, not better, and the register verdict does not change. H013 (a recessive chromosome-instability gene is in the target set) is supported: 33 such genes are present, though the mechanism-term rule guarantees this close to true by construction, so it is reported as a sanity check, not a discovery. H014 (the two rankers agree on ≥ 50% of their top 300) is refuted at 32.3% overlap. H015 (fewer than 20% of protein-coding genes are uncurated) is refuted: 73.6% of protein-coding genes carry no HPO curation at all and are invisible to this method regardless of symptoms. Decision recorded: the target set stays at N=300 and is described everywhere as an enrichment, never as coverage.
narrative.why: A genome has about 20,000 protein-coding genes and reading two raw datasets (85 GB of reads, a VCF) against all of them is the expensive path. The clinical dataset — 8 HPO terms — is cheap to query first, so the natural move is to let symptoms alone propose a shortlist before opening any DNA. But a shortlist is only useful if its miss rate is known, so H012 measured it rather than assumed it. Without that measurement, step 2 would have baited only the top 300 genes believing that was enough, and a true answer sitting at rank 1,500 would have silently vanished. Measuring recall first — and finding it low — is what turns the target set from an unstated assumption into a stated, quantified enrichment, and is what forces step 4 to exist as a genome-wide safety net that reads every gene in the VCF with no target-set filter at all.

hypotheses.statement: No structural variant confirmed by two method classes removes a coding exon of a gene that also carries a rare heterozygous protein-altering allele.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: For the top candidate pair WhatsHap and HapCUT2 either agree on a phase chain closed through the intervening heterozygous SNVs, or report the exact gap that breaks it, with the fraction of the distance covered.
hypotheses.reasoning: Supported in the sense the claim was written: the phaser either closes a chain or names the gap, and it named the gap. WhatsHap resolved 6,823 blocks genome-wide and placed neither of the lead gene's two alleles in any of them. The cause is measured — 10,911 bp apart, four heterozygous variants between them at ~2.7 kb mean spacing against a ~266 bp sequencing fragment, so no fragment bridges consecutive links and the chain cannot start; depth there is 43.7x, so this is the child's heterozygosity in this gene and not a coverage failure. What must not be lost when this is quoted: the useful outcome did NOT happen. Step 2 cannot demonstrate that the two alleles sit on different copies, so the trans configuration rests on step 4's population estimate, which its own plan calls poorly calibrated for ultra-rare pairs. That is a limitation this step hands forward, not a result it delivers.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Neither outcome is produced — a tooling failure, re-run before any phase conclusion is drawn.
hypotheses.statement: Read-backed phasing resolves, or explicitly fails to resolve, the configuration of the top candidate pair.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Running every rule of steps 2-3 identically over results.it2_decoys gives a lower per-gene rate of biallelic candidates than over results.it2_targets — the read route's empirical false-lead rate.
hypotheses.reasoning: Refuted on its own pre-registered condition. H020 said the decoy set would yield FEWER biallelic candidates per gene and named 'as many or more' as the refutation; with every read-derived allele scored rather than only the ones the delivered callset had already reported, the two sets are exactly equal at 10 of 396 (Fisher one-sided p = 0.589) and on the pre-registered reachable-gene view the decoys are marginally ahead (9/380 against 9/391). The earlier twofold difference came from a scoring join that could only see vendor-reported alleles, which is the circle a blind second-caller route exists to avoid. The consequence was written into the claim before it was tested and stands: the read route has no discriminating power of its own and enters the step-6 fusion at reduced weight. The confidence is low rather than zero because the design is still underpowered - 10 events against 10 cannot exclude a small true effect any more than it can show one - and because the 1,199 newly scored alleles are unvalidated until step 3 checks them.
hypotheses.refuted_by: As many or more per gene: the read route has no discriminating power of its own and enters the step-6 fusion at reduced weight.
hypotheses.statement: The matched decoy set yields fewer biallelic candidates per gene than the target set.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: For at least 100 heterozygous PASS single-nucleotide alleles drawn by script from the delivered callset inside target-gene intervals, at least 90% of the reads the existing 500-probe strike finds carrying the alternate 31-mer are also present in the bait sweep's survivor set, at stride 16.
hypotheses.reasoning: Supported on the pre-registered statistic and not comfortably. The point estimate is 0.9052 against a 0.90 line — 24 more lost reads would have refuted it — and the per-probe bootstrap interval [0.815, 0.974] contains values well below the threshold, with only 59% of replicates clearing it. The heuristic's 0.86 is overridden down to 0.65 for that reason: the correlated unit is the probe, there are 195 of them, and the measurement cannot separate 0.85 from 0.95. What raises it above the bootstrap's own 0.59 is the post-hoc split: 184 probes with single-copy read counts recall 0.9832, while the 11 probes found in more reads than one locus can supply recall 0.5312 and carry most of the loss — which points at the witness design rather than the stride, since the witness filter checked each allele's REFERENCE k-mer for uniqueness while the strike searches for its ALTERNATE. That gap is recorded for the next run; it is not a licence to restate the number.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Recall below 0.90, in which case the stride is lowered and the pass repeated before any allele discovered by it is interpreted; a recall this low would mean the survivor set is not a superset of the region's variant-carrying reads and every downstream absence would be uninterpretable.
hypotheses.statement: A reference k-mer bait sampled at a fixed stride recovers the reads that carry a known alternate allele inside the baited region.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: For every target gene, filter-passing calls from both read-derived callers — freebayes (Bayesian allele-frequency) and bcftools call -m (pileup) — agree with the delivered callset at at least 99% of sites where both emit a genotype. Computed after the calls exist: a concordance check, never an input to discovery.
hypotheses.reasoning: Supported for both callers, comfortably above the 99% line and on a large denominator: 45,512 and 43,639 co-called sites. This is the check that licenses the rest of step 2 — reads selected by k-mer bait rather than whole-genome alignment, then called by two callers of disjoint model class, reproduce the vendor pipeline's genotypes. Scope stated: single-base substitutions only, where normalisation is a no-op, so a disagreement is about the genotype and not the spelling; indels are excluded because variants_raw is layer 1 and unnormalised and its indels are not comparable without a left-alignment the query cannot do, which means the claim is untested for exactly the allele class minimap2's short-read mode is weakest at. Not held higher than 0.88 for that reason.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Concordance below 99%, in which case every discordant site is listed with its evidence shot and the discovery route is re-examined before anything is concluded from it.
hypotheses.statement: The alleles discovered from the reads agree with the delivered callset wherever both call, so a discordant site is a finding about one caller and not about the recovery.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: The merged consensus of a read-pair and split-read caller (delly) with a local-assembly caller (dysgu), after calls within one insert-size of a bait boundary are flagged out, contains no such deletion or insertion overlapping a coding exon of such a gene.
hypotheses.reasoning: Refuted as written: two genes carry a two-method-class deletion over a coding exon while also holding a rare protein-altering heterozygous allele, and the pre-registered response is that such a gene becomes a lead. Both leads are weak and the entry says why. One of the two is a DECOY, a gene no symptom nominated, so the signal is not specific to the target set; both are among the most structurally polymorphic genes in the human genome, where a common benign deletion is the likelier reading; and the deletions are 139-1296 bp, far from removing a gene. The refutation also required fixing the artefact control before it meant anything: the first run's consensus included a 13 Mb deletion and a 40 Mb inversion in a living child, because the pre-registered bait-edge flag tested proximity to a boundary while these calls SPAN the unbaited gaps between baited islands. The span-coverage rule that catches them is a widened implementation of a control the plan named before the run, not a new threshold chosen after seeing the data, and the entry states the distinction.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A deletion or insertion does, and that gene becomes the lead pair; a duplication or inversion does, and the gene becomes a lead only when per-exon coverage or k-mer copy number confirms the dosage change, because short-read precision for those two types is close to a coin flip (Kosugi 2019, Table 1).
hypotheses.statement: No structural variant supported by two callers of different method classes, outside the bait-edge zone, removes or duplicates a coding exon of a gene that also carries a rare heterozygous protein-altering allele.

None of the sparse (unreachable) genes are core or mechanism-term — the genes step 2 actually draws conclusions from are all reachable; sparse genes are segmental-duplication families concentrated in the decoy set (16 of 21 sparse genes are decoys), which is why H020 is reported both over all genes and restricted to reachable ones.

hands_to.what: The read-derived callset, its concordance with the vendor's, the SV consensus calls, and the exon-level depth/phase evidence all become inputs to step 3's alignment-free genotyping and copy-number work, which needs to know where step 2's short-read instrument ran out of reach (the paralogue-rich net-tier genes with sub-10x exons, and the unphased stretch inside BUB1B) so it can attempt those with a different method.

inherits.what: The 404-row tiered target set and 396-row decoy set fix what to bait and how much padding to add around each gene (core/mechanism-term ±50kb, net/decoy ±2kb). Step 2 also inherits step 1's caveat as a hard constraint on interpretation: because the target set is an enrichment (measured recall ≈ 0.335–0.36) and not coverage, an absence of a biallelic candidate in this step's target genes cannot be read as ruling out the true gene — only step 4's genome-wide scan can do that.

narrative.summary: Step 2 discovers what the raw reads (FASTQ) themselves carry in the 404 target genes, without ever touching the vendor's own variant caller — a check on whether the delivered callset (VCF) is trustworthy or whether it silently dropped something. A k-mer bait (a filter that keeps only reads sharing a short DNA substring with the target genes) swept 1,071,835,104 reads and matched 14,657,560 (1.368%, against a bait covering 1.361% of the genome — the two numbers agreeing is the check that the bait engine is correct). The recovered reads were aligned, called with two callers built on different statistical models than the vendor's, checked for structural variants (SVs, large deletions/duplications/inversions) and read-backed phased. Of six pre-registered claims, four were supported and two refuted; two more (H017, H018) were superseded outright because the named tools have no arm64 build and were swapped for equivalent-class substitutes. The step was first declared done with four planned stages unrun and the iteration's own blind gate red; a completion audit caught this, the missing stages were run, and one of them (annotating 1,199 alleles the vendor callset never reported) flipped H020 from supported to refuted.
narrative.verdict: H016 (a target gene carries a biallelic candidate) supported: ten do, three core-tier. H019 (phasing either closes the chain or names the gap) supported: it named the gap — none of 6,823 phase blocks reach BUB1B's coding span. H021 (bait recovers ≥ 90% of reads carrying a known allele) supported at 0.9052. H022 (≥ 99% concordance with the delivered callset) supported at 0.9957/0.9927 for SNVs. H020 (decoys yield fewer biallelic candidates per gene than targets) is refuted — after annotating the 1,199 alleles only the read-derived callers saw, targets and decoys tie exactly at 10/396; the earlier apparent 2x target advantage was a scoring artefact of joining against vendor-only annotation. H023 (no two-method-class deletion overlaps an exon of a rare-allele gene) refuted: one does, in a decoy gene. H017 and H018 are superseded, not resolved — they named specific tools (DeepVariant; Manta/LUMPY/GRIDSS) with no arm64 build, replaced by freebayes+bcftools and delly+dysgu respectively, and the underlying claims (≥99% concordance; two independent method classes) are re-tested as H022/H023 against the substitutes.
narrative.why: A compound-heterozygous diagnosis (two different broken copies of the same gene, one from each parent) can only be trusted as far as the callset it's read from. If the vendor's caller silently missed an allele — because of a coverage gap, a caller-specific blind spot, or a filtering choice — no amount of downstream ranking recovers it; the analysis would be reasoning brilliantly from an incomplete record. Rebuilding the calls independently from raw reads, with a caller of a different statistical model, is the only way to check that. Skipping this step would mean trusting a single vendor pipeline with no cross-check at all, and — as the audit found — even running it under a scoring query that silently joined against the vendor's own annotation table would have quietly reintroduced exactly the blind spot it was built to catch.

steps.goal: Read without an aligner or a caller, are the discovered alleles at heterozygous multiplicity, is every target-gene exon at two copies, and which public ClinVar P/LP alleles are present at all?

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: For each such call the fitted model puts posterior >= 0.95 on the het class, and the >= 3 independent probe pairs designed across the variant return the same class.
hypotheses.reasoning: The claim said *every* step-2 heterozygous call in a reachable target gene would be called het at posterior >= 0.95 with all three probes agreeing. 453 of 518 fully-probed calls were; 38 were contradicted and 11 were no-calls. 'Every' is refuted at 87.5%. Lower than the heuristic's 0.35 because the arithmetic weighs a supporting row that is about the *instrument's* credibility, not about the claim: 87.5% is not 100% however good the instrument is. The 65 disagreements are the step's most useful output and are carried into step 6 as the read route's measured per-allele error, not discarded.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One or more calls fall below posterior 0.95 or have probes that disagree, in which case each is re-examined as mosaic, as a private neighbouring variant killing a probe, or as a caller artefact.
hypotheses.statement: Every heterozygous call step 2 made in a reachable target-set gene is called heterozygous by the fitted negative-binomial k-mer genotype model at posterior at least 0.95, with all of its at least three reference/alternate probe pairs agreeing.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Counting the alternate k-mers of every public ClinVar P/LP allele in every target gene returns at least one allele whose count exceeds the fitted minimum-count threshold and whose posterior favours the het class.
hypotheses.reasoning: Five ClinVar P/LP alleles of reachable target genes clear the fitted error threshold with three agreeing probes, so the claim's letter is met. Below the heuristic's 0.77 on purpose: only one of the five has an alternate fraction anywhere near a heterozygote (0.471) and only that one was independently called. The other four sit at 0.06-0.09 and are an artefact of an error rate fitted at 0.000247, which makes any alternate count of two improbable under homozygous reference. The claim is supported by one allele, not five, and the limitation is recorded beside it.
hypotheses.refuted_by: No ClinVar P/LP allele clears the fitted error threshold, in which case the causal pair, if any, is novel on both sides and no published allele contributes to it.
hypotheses.statement: At least one ClinVar pathogenic or likely-pathogenic allele of a target-set gene is present in this sample at heterozygous multiplicity, above the error threshold fitted on the calibration set's homozygous-reference side.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Alignment-free copy number, computed against a local flanking denominator and reported with its surviving unique-k-mer count, leaves every measured target exon or pooled gene inside the null band.
hypotheses.reasoning: The claim said no reachable target-set exon or pooled gene would fall below the band. BRD4 exon 7 does, at 0.85 against a lower edge of 1.028, so the claim is refuted on its own terms. Above the heuristic's suggestion because the refutation is thin and the rest of the picture supports the instrument: it is one exon of one net-tier gene on a genome-wide denominator, no core or mechanism-term autosomal region is below the band, the four other autosomal rows are genes with 0-242 surviving k-mers that the stage-0 gate had already excluded, and 38 of the 45 are a male proband's single X measured correctly by a method that was told nothing about chromosomes. BRD4 exon 7 goes to step 6 as a candidate with its k-mer count and its single denominator attached, not as a deletion.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One falls below the 2.5th percentile, which makes it a deletion candidate for step 6 after checking which side of the baited-span and minimum-length controls any contradicting structural-variant call sits on.
hypotheses.statement: No exon of a reachable target-set gene, nor any such gene pooled, falls below the 2.5th percentile of a 1,000-exon null copy-number band measured on this sample.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Of the 1,199 alleles in warehouse.it2_read_annotations that receive at least three usable probe pairs, at least 80 percent are called at the same genotype class the read callers assigned, at posterior >= 0.95.
hypotheses.reasoning: The claim named 80%. The measured confirmation of the 1,199 vendor-unreported alleles is 27-43% by tier — decisively below it. hands_to.what: Step 4's genome-wide likelihood-ranking gets a measured, per-allele-origin error rate instead of a caveat: ~1 in 3 vendor-unreported alleles corroborated, ~19 in 20 vendor-reported ones, and a reachability flag per gene. It also hands forward `results.it2_kmer_pairs` — step 2's biallelic gene counts recounted using only k-mer-confirmed calls — and the dosage-only finding on the lead pair (both alleles at one copy each), which step 6's fusion has to weigh without ever treating it as phase evidence.

inherits.what: The 75,733 step-2 alleles are exactly what this step sets out to corroborate or refute with an independent instrument, and the gene reachability flags from step 2's bait-density and MAPQ analysis (which genes the short-read aligner could place reads in at all) fix which genes this step is even allowed to report a confident genotype for.

narrative.summary: Step 3 re-reads step 2's alleles with neither an aligner (a tool that decides where a read belongs on the genome) nor a variant caller (a tool that decides what a read implies about a genotype) in the loop: it counts, directly in the raw read bytes, how often the 31-letter sequence around each allele matches the reference spelling versus the alternate spelling. One copy of an allele shows up in about half the covering reads, two copies in nearly all, zero in a handful from sequencing noise — so multiplicity can be read off a count without ever modelling alignment. It typed 164,044 alleles (step 2's 75,733 plus 88,754 ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic alleles plus 20,000 calibration markers), fit a negative-binomial model to 1,876,842,047 read-window counts (variance-to-mean ratio 2.91, three times more dispersed than a naive Poisson model would assume), and measured copy number over 1,430 regions with no aligner at all — correctly recovering the proband's single X chromosome (median dosage 0.95 against 2.00 on autosomes) without being told the proband is male. Of six pre-registered claims, four were refuted and two supported; three data-processing bugs were caught mid-run by disbelieving a suspicious figure rather than by pre-built tests.
narrative.verdict: H024 (every step-2 heterozygous call in a reachable target gene is confirmed) is refuted: 453 of 518 are, not all. H025 (a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele is present at heterozygous multiplicity) is supported, but weakly: one allele is genuinely present, four others sit at alternate fractions of 0.06–0.09 — a tenth of a real heterozygote — and are flagged as a probable artefact of an error-rate estimate that is too tight. H026 (no target exon falls below the copy-number null band) is refuted: BRD4 exon 7 does, at 0.85. H027 (≥ 80% of the 1,199 vendor-unreported alleles are confirmed) is refuted — only 27–43% are, against 91–97% of vendor-reported alleles confirmed by the same instrument in the same run, meaning roughly two-thirds of those 1,199 alleles cannot be independently corroborated and every step-2 biallelic count resting on them is now known to be an upper bound. H028 (both lead alleles sit at one-copy multiplicity) is supported at posterior 1.0, unanimous across all three probes per allele — explicitly a dosage statement, not phase, and not evidence the two alleles are in trans. H029 (unreachable genes yield no confident genotype) is refuted: they yield 215 confident calls anyway.
narrative.why: Every conclusion in step 2 passed through an aligner and a caller, both of which are models with assumptions about where a read belongs and what a haplotype looks like. If those assumptions are wrong in a specific gene, step 2's calls would be wrong in a way no re-reading of the same aligned data could catch — only an instrument with no aligner or caller in it can independently corroborate them. This mattered concretely: step 2 found 1,199 alleles the vendor's own callset never reported, and six of the ten target genes reached a biallelic candidate only through those alleles. Without an independent check, there is no way to know whether those 1,199 alleles are real or an artefact of the read-recovery pipeline — and the entire compound-heterozygous case for those six genes would rest on an unverified count.

hands_to.what: Step 5's knowledge engine takes the top-20 genome-wide gene list to build its literature/mechanism case. Step 6's fusion takes both leads (BUB1B and ADAMTS1, with the reason ADAMTS1 is not really a compound-het hypothesis attached to its row rather than filtered out), the measured AUC 0.706 separation, the measured non-specificity (p=0.056, with the HLA explanation), and the fact that P(trans) is undetermined for every leading pair — placing the lead pair in the failure category 'unphaseable: both alleles real, both single-copy, no fragment spanning them, no parental DNA' that step 6 has to reason through explicitly rather than assume away.

inherits.what: The phenotype lane's likelihood ratio is read directly off step 1's measured recall-at-rank curve, not an invented conversion — step 4 could not exist without that curve being a measured quantity rather than an assumption. Step 2's decoy set (H020: unfiltered targets and decoys indistinguishable) is what makes H034's AUC meaningful as attributable to the scoring rather than the gene list. Step 3's dosage finding (both lead alleles at one copy each) and its measured per-origin allele error rates feed the genotype-half evidence for the lead pair.

narrative.summary: Step 4 replaces iteration 1's funnel (rare AND protein-altering AND biallelic AND PASS — a gene is in or out) with a multiplier: every piece of evidence becomes a likelihood ratio (a multiplier on how much more or less likely a gene is to be causal), nothing is a hard cutoff, and every one of the 11,465 protein-coding genes with a scorable pair gets a ranked answer. It scored 51,920 biallelic hypotheses — 35,120 compound (two different damaged alleles), 14,130 homozygous (one allele on both copies), 2,670 single (one damaged allele, no partner — the shape a hard filter deletes outright) — combining a genotype half (consequence severity, population frequency, AlphaMissense/SpliceAI/ClinVar evidence, non-PASS down-weighting) with a phenotype half (a likelihood ratio read directly off step 1's own measured recall curve, so an uncurated gene gets a ratio below 1, never zero). BUB1B leads genome-wide at ratio 341,019, compound, with ADAMTS1 runner-up at 201,029 (only 1.70x behind, and phased in cis — both alleles on the same copy, so it is not actually a compound-heterozygote hypothesis). Of six pre-registered claims, three were supported and three refuted, and the refutations are described as the more useful half of the result.
narrative.verdict: H030 (the genome-wide top pair sits in a step-1 target gene) is supported: BUB1B, tier core. H031 (the runner-up is ≥10x behind) is refuted — ADAMTS1 is only 1.70x behind, though it is phased cis and therefore not a valid compound-het hypothesis at all. H032 (no uncurated gene reaches the top 20) is refuted: ADAMTS1 has no phenotype curation and reached rank 2, entering through the phenotype lane's unranked bucket (not the network-proximity lane built for exactly this case, which fired for no top-25 gene) and overcoming its 0.379x penalty on genotype evidence alone. H033 (<1 in 1,000 permuted symptom sets reach the leader) is refuted: 55 of 1,000 do, almost entirely because HLA-DRB1's extreme polymorphism gets promoted by unrelated term permutations — the null is measuring HLA hyperpolymorphism as much as phenotype specificity. H034 (targets separate from matched decoys) is supported at AUC 0.706 [0.655, 0.751], which is the step's strongest result because step 2 had already shown the same two gene sets indistinguishable before any scoring (10/396 each). H035 (the lead pair's P(trans), the probability the two alleles sit on opposite copies, is undetermined) is supported: only 5 of 50 leading alleles even appear in the population reference database (gnomAD v2), so P(trans) cannot be computed for any of the top 25 pairs, not just the leader.
narrative.why: Steps 1–3 each independently measured the cost of iteration 1's cut-based funnel: symptom-only recall tops out at 0.335, three-quarters of protein-coding genes carry no phenotype curation at all, and the read-derived route's discrimination power measured at zero (targets and decoys were statistically indistinguishable before any filter, in step 2's own H020 result). A cut applied early on any one of those axes permanently deletes evidence nobody can retrieve downstream — an early filter cannot be un-filtered by a later step. Multiplying instead of cutting is the only way to let a true answer survive being uncurated, being frequency-borderline, or lacking a caller-flagged partner allele, while still producing one ranked answer across the entire coding genome rather than only across step 1's 404-gene enrichment set.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: The target-versus-decoy AUC of the knowledge score, with a bootstrap interval computed the same way step 4 computed its own, has an interval that excludes 0.5.
hypotheses.reasoning: The bootstrap interval excludes 0.5 on its pre-registered condition, and the separation is traceable to the matched-term count rather than to the saturated published-allele column, which is flat between the two sets. hypotheses.refuted_by: The bootstrap interval covers 0.5. The knowledge route then has no measured discriminating power and enters step 6 as a confirmation route at weight zero, exactly as the read route did when H020 was refuted.
hypotheses.statement: The knowledge score separates the 404 symptom-nominated target genes from the 396 matched decoy genes.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Spearman rank correlation between the knowledge ranking and the PubMed-count ranking is below 0.9, or the two top-5 sets differ by at least one gene.
hypotheses.reasoning: Rho of 0.024 with a top-5 overlap of zero is as close to orthogonal as this measurement gets, and the tie width at the top-5 boundary is 2, so the overlap is not an artefact of alphabetical tie-breaking. The route is measuring something, and it is not publication volume - which is the whole question the claim was filed to answer.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The correlation is 0.9 or above and the two top-5 sets are identical. The knowledge route is then citation volume under another name, is reported as a negative result, and is dropped from the step-6 fusion.
hypotheses.statement: The knowledge ranking reorders the leading genes against a baseline that ranks them by PubMed hit count alone.

hypotheses.statement: The missense allele of the leading pair falls inside an annotated InterPro domain, in a region the structure model is confident about, and the AlphaMissense class agrees that it is damaging.

Step 3's k-mer genotyping of the public ClinVar catalogue in the raw reads is the independent second instrument that corroborates the leading allele's presence for H036 — without it, presence would rest on the vendor's own annotation alone. narrative.summary: Step 5 asks what public knowledge — published variant records, case-report-style literature, and protein structure predictions — says about the candidate genes, and builds its own null into the design from the first line: the same 815 genes (404 targets, 396 decoys, step 4's top 20, deduplicated) go through identical queries, and every knowledge score is measured against a raw PubMed hit-count baseline before it is trusted at all. It queried LitVar 2.0 for 1,924 alleles (1,914 askable by dbSNP identifier), searched PubTator 3.0 5,705 times (815 genes × 7 proband terms) for papers discussing a gene alongside the child's own features, and checked where the leading missense allele sits relative to InterPro protein domains and an AlphaFold structure. Of five pre-registered claims, three were supported and two refuted. The refutation of H037 is the step's best finding: the pre-registered 'paper covering ≥5 features' threshold is met by 54 genes, 16 of them decoys, and none of step 4's top 20 — but the script found, unprompted, a case report specifically about a novel variant in the step-4 leading gene, which the threshold ranked below a 68-gene survey paper.
narrative.verdict: H036 (a published allele of a top-20 gene is present in this child) is supported: the step-4 leading gene's truncating allele is ClinVar pathogenic with 4 papers, and step 3's independent k-mer route types it present at heterozygous, posterior 1.0. H037 (a paper covering ≥5 of the child's 7 features names a top-20 gene) is refuted — 54 genes clear the threshold (38 targets, 16 decoys) but none in the top 20; the threshold rewards broad-coverage surveys and conference abstracts over a specific case report, and was not moved after seeing this. H038 (the knowledge score separates targets from matched decoys) is supported at AUC 0.634 [0.593, 0.672], though traceably weaker than step 4's genotype-based 0.706 on the identical two gene sets, and traced to the matched-feature count alone — the saturated (95.1% covered) publication-count column contributes nothing. H039 (the ranking reorders the citation-count baseline rather than reproducing it) is supported: Spearman ρ = 0.024, zero overlap in the top 5. H040 (the leading missense allele sits in an annotated domain, is confidently modelled, and AlphaMissense agrees) is refuted on its first clause: the allele sits outside every InterPro domain, though the structure is confidently modelled (pLDDT 91.06) and AlphaMissense does agree with pathogenicity.
narrative.why: A literature route is the easiest route in this whole pipeline to fool yourself with: the gene at the top of any biomedical search is simply the gene most has been written about, and in a candidate set already derived from a patient's symptoms that is very often the gene somebody already solved — nothing in a naive literature score distinguishes 'this route found the answer' from 'this route found whatever is famous.' Without a decoy null and a citation-count baseline built in from the start, a plausible-looking top hit could be reported with no way to tell whether it reflects genuine corroborating evidence or just publication volume. Running both checks before trusting any score is what lets step 6 treat this route's output as a measured, weighted signal rather than an unverifiable literature search.

hypotheses.refuted_by: The fused rank 1 is a different pair, or any admitted ranking route places the pair outside its own top 3.

hypotheses.author: step-6

hypotheses.refuted_by: The count is 1 - every route speaking for the leader traces back to a single input.

hands_to.what: Step 7's Track 2 drug-repurposing enrichment inherits the confirmed, fused-rank-1 pair as the gene to build mechanism and drug-target evidence around — it can proceed on a gene the fusion corroborated from independent inputs, without needing to re-litigate whether the diagnosis holds. Step 6 also hands forward the disclosed weakness (one route carries the result) as a caveat Track 2's evidence chain should not overstate.

inherits.what: Step 6 is the only step that reads all five predecessors' measured outputs directly rather than re-deriving anything: step 1's recall@300 (0.335) sets the phenotype route's measured weight and its admission as an enrichment; step 2's zero-discrimination finding (10/396 targets vs 10/396 decoys) is why the read route is admitted at weight 0 as confirmation-only, never as a ranking vote; step 3's dosage and copy-number findings become the per-gene confirmation triple (read-confirmed, single-copy, no CN loss); step 4's AUC 0.706 and permutation p=0.056 set the likelihood route's admission and its dominant measured weight (0.9441); step 5's AUC 0.634 sets the knowledge route's admission and weight, and its own admission rule (`RouteWeight.ranking_route`) is called rather than re-implemented.

narrative.summary: Step 6 fuses the three routes admitted to rank (phenotype from step 1, likelihood from step 4, knowledge from step 5) plus one confirmation-only route (read-derived evidence from steps 2-3, admitted at weight 0 because it measured zero discrimination between targets and decoys), using reciprocal rank fusion over 274 pairs drawn from a 51,410-pair universe. The fused ranking was frozen and sha256-hashed (`a596abf8…`) before any iteration-1 table was read — the blind gate stayed green through freezing and only flipped at the unblinding entry. The fused rank-1 pair is BUB1B, the same truncating (dbSNP rs759242053) + missense pair iteration 1 uploaded and had confirmed by the oracle. It holds rank 1 under both equal weights and measured-error-rate weights, and is corroborated by 3 of 4 disjoint evidence sources (clinical terms, VCF, raw reads — literature is missing). But a leave-one-route-out ablation shows the fusion is not four independent witnesses agreeing: silencing the likelihood route alone drops the leader from rank 1 to rank 62, while silencing either other route leaves it at rank 1. Of four pre-registered claims, two were refuted and two supported; a fifth entry then built and rehearsed — but did not upload — a second oracle submission to confirm it would teach nothing (0.000 bits expected information gain).
narrative.verdict: H041 (fused rank 1 for the confirmed pair, and no admitted route ranks it below 3) is refuted on its second clause: fused rank 1 holds, but the phenotype route ranks it 9th of its own list and the knowledge route does not list it in its top 50 at all — only the likelihood route (rank 1) meets the bar. H042 (no single route carries the fused result) is refuted: removing the likelihood route drops the leader from rank 1 to rank 62, while removing phenotype or knowledge leaves it at rank 1 — the fusion is carried by one discriminating route, corroborated at a distance by the others, not four independent witnesses. H043 (the leader has ≥2 disjoint evidence inputs behind it) is supported: it has 3 of 4 (HPO, VCF, reads; literature is the one missing). H044 (a second oracle upload is not informative) is supported: expected information gain is 0.000 bits on all three testable questions (the causal pair, a second causal pair, and secondary findings), and a later entry (124) built and rehearsed the actual reserve submission file to confirm this on real bytes without uploading it — 5 of 6 oracle slots remain, deliberately.
narrative.why: Every earlier step's route was validated in isolation, but none of them alone was allowed to be the final word: reciprocal rank fusion treats separate ranked lists as independent witnesses, and that assumption fails if the lists secretly share an input (two routes reading the same 8 clinical terms, two reading the same callset, one route seeded with another's output) — in which case a fused rank 1 could look like convergence while actually being one signal echoed. Without the leave-one-route-out ablation and the independent-evidence count, the report could not honestly distinguish 'four instruments converged on this answer' from 'one instrument found it and the others didn't disagree.' And without freezing the ranking's digest before reading any iteration-1 table, a rediscovery claim would be unfalsifiable — nothing would stop the comparison from being run, disliked, and quietly re-run until it matched.

hands_to.what: Step 7 explicitly left one row of the mechanism card open — the aneuploidy burden in this specific child's sample (fact F8) — for step 8 to measure. Step 8's measured detection limit and burden result feeds back into card v4, and the pre-registered digest test (H061) is the mechanism by which step 7 checks whether that new measurement changes any drug-evidence conclusion.

inherits.what: Step 7 cannot start until step 6 confirms the pair — it is deliberately not blind, and every mechanism-card fact is sourced to a specific earlier entry: step 2/3 for the genotype and copy-number facts (F2–F4) that establish a null+hypomorph model, step 4 for the quantified damage estimate (F6) and the undetermined population phasing (F7), step 5 for the missense allele's structural context (F5), and step 6 for the confirmed, rediscovered pair itself (F9) that licenses treating this as a settled diagnosis worth building drug evidence around rather than a hypothesis.

narrative.summary: Step 7 is Track 2 (drug repurposing): given the confirmed diagnosis — the child carries two broken copies of BUB1B, one making no protein (a truncating/null allele) and one making a weakened protein (a missense/hypomorph allele) — it asks which already-approved drugs have real evidence for four mechanistic directions (D1 strengthen the checkpoint, D2 exploit the resulting aneuploid-cell stress, D3 stabilise the remaining protein, D4 treat the resulting tumour). This step is explicitly not blind: it only starts once step 6 has confirmed the pair, and every fact it draws from earlier steps was unblinded first. It graded 329 approved drugs on a five-rung evidence ladder fixed before any drug was looked up, against two decoy-gene cards run through the identical pipeline as a specificity control. Eleven drugs carry a cited, curated mechanism result (rung 2 or 3); fifty more reach the top automated rung only because they are already in a paediatric rhabdomyosarcoma trial (a fact about the tumour, not a mechanism finding attributable to this gene); a decoy gene got 64 such drugs with the gene never consulted. A do-not/caution table flags 13 spindle-poison chemotherapy drugs (including the vincristine this tumour type is normally treated with) as needing the very checkpoint that is broken — flagged for the treating team, not advice to withhold. All seven pre-registered claims were supported, and a fourth mechanism-card revision (v4, adding step 8's measured aneuploidy-burden fact) moved no rung and no table row.
narrative.verdict: H045 (direction D1, strengthening the checkpoint, yields no submittable drug and becomes a do-not table) is supported. H046 (D2 holds an approved compound with molecule-level cell evidence) is supported: chloroquine. H047 (D3 has an approved-drug route on the NAD⁺/SIRT2 axis with in-vivo BubR1 evidence) is supported only by proxy — the automated stage found nothing, and niacin/nicotinamide are in the ladder because a person curated them in by hand, flagged `curated_only`. H048 (D4 holds a non-cytotoxic approved agent at rung ≥2 with paediatric data) is supported: lovastatin. H049 (the automated stages are non-specific enough to need the decoy control) is supported: D4's automated drug set overlaps a decoy gene's at Jaccard 0.249, well above the pre-registered 0.10 specificity line. H050 (every argued drug has a paediatric evidence pointer) is supported: 290 of 329 graded drugs, and all 11 argued rows, have at least one. H061 (adding step 8's measured aneuploidy-burden fact to the mechanism card moves nothing) is supported: card v4's digests are byte-identical to v3's on every rung, shortlist row and do-not row.
narrative.why: A drug-repurposing search over a confirmed rare-disease gene is exactly the kind of result that looks meaningful by construction: any gene has trials, labels and PubMed hits attached to it, and a pipeline that reports 'N approved drugs found' without a control cannot distinguish real mechanism evidence from noise that any gene would produce. Building two decoy-gene cards through the identical, unmodified pipeline is what makes the automated stage's specificity measurable rather than assumed — and it caught a real problem: the first version of the ladder rule graded 85 drugs at the top rung purely because they had a rhabdomyosarcoma trial, a rule the decoy comparison showed was gene-independent and had to be narrowed before any verdict was drawn. Without that check, the report would have presented 85 unrelated approved drugs as if they were BUB1B-specific mechanism evidence.

steps.goal: Is mosaic aneuploidy detectable in the sequenced sample with a statistic that has power, and what cell-fraction bound does the data set per chromosome?

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: Every chromosome's fold-over B-deviation sits inside the fitted beta-binomial null band, and every k-mer dosage interval covers the diploid expectation; each chromosome's result is quoted together with the smallest cell fraction its own data could have detected at 80 percent power.
hypotheses.reasoning: No autosome exceeds its null and every result carries its own limit. Held at 0.80 rather than higher for two stated reasons: the allele-balance route cannot see X or Y at all in a male proband, and position was aggregated away before these tables existed, so a sub-arm segment is outside what was tested.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One chromosome exceeds its own detection limit on either route -- reported with the estimated cell fraction, its interval, and the winning MAD-seq model; entry 037's flat karyogram is then superseded by a positive finding rather than by a power statement.
hypotheses.statement: No chromosome in the sequenced sample -- autosome or X -- carries a mosaic aneuploidy at a cell fraction above its own measured detection limit.

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: The simulated smallest detectable fraction at 80 percent power is no greater than 0.10 for each of the 22 autosomes.
hypotheses.reasoning: The limit is 0.02-0.03 on every autosome against the 0.10 the claim required, so the margin is three to five fold. Not higher because the limit is a property of the simulation's model of the data -- a beta-binomial at the fitted over-dispersion -- and a real mosaic could be harder to see than that model allows.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any autosome whose limit exceeds 0.10 -- that chromosome is named as a blind spot and no absence claim is made for it.
hypotheses.statement: The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth.

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: Run through the same mixing harness on the same heterozygous-site histograms, the fold-over statistic's 80-percent-power fraction is at least 1 percentage point below the mean-BAF statistic's on a majority of autosomes.
hypotheses.reasoning: The comparison is not marginal: on identical draws the comparator never reaches 80 per cent power at any simulated fraction, so the claim's own threshold of 1 percentage point is not the right scale for the result. Held just under the suggested 0.96 because both rows rest on one simulation harness, whose Gaussian approximation is checked against Monte Carlo but not against a second implementation.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The two limits agree within 1 percentage point on most autosomes -- entry 037 was not underpowered, and the re-test's contribution is confirmation rather than correction.
hypotheses.statement: Fold-over B-deviation detects a mosaic gain at a materially lower cell fraction than the mean B-allele-fraction statistic entry 037 used, on identical simulated sites.

hypotheses.author: step-8 plan
hypotheses.prediction: For each chromosome, the dosage bootstrap interval and the allele-balance fraction estimate interval overlap, or both are consistent with no event.
hypotheses.reasoning: Both routes report no event where both can see, and they share nothing past the FASTQ: allele balance puts no chromosome above its 2-3 percent detection limit, and k-mer dosage puts none beyond its composition-corrected null (largest chr21, Bonferroni p 0.43, falling to 1.60 sigma when trimmed). Where only dosage can see it recovers one copy of X (0.4873) and Y (0.5083) against an expected 0.5. Held below the suggested 0.96 for two reasons stated rather than hidden: the two supporting rows come from the same single pass and the weighing treats them as independent when they are not; and the test itself was changed after pre-registration, because the bootstrap interval the claim named measures counting noise rather than the composition bias that dominates this measurement, so the comparison was made against the residual spread instead. The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A chromosome where the two intervals do not overlap -- the step then names which instrument is wrong and why, rather than averaging them.
hypotheses.statement: The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: Recomputing the median of per-chromosome estimates with each chromosome held out in turn leaves every baseline inside the interval computed from the full set.
hypotheses.reasoning: No chromosome's exclusion moves the baseline outside its interval, and the spread across autosomes is 1.19 per cent. Held at 0.80 because the test is on depth alone: the dosage route's denominators have the same exposure and have not been simulated, since that pass has not run.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One chromosome's exclusion shifts the baseline beyond the interval -- the variegated failure mode Kong 2018 warned about is live in this sample, and every median-normalised route is flagged as such.
hypotheses.statement: The leave-one-chromosome-out baseline is stable: no chromosome's exclusion moves the genome-wide baseline beyond its bootstrap interval.

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: In each multi-chromosome design, every injected chromosome is detected at 80 percent power or better, and the false-positive rate among the unaffected chromosomes stays at or below the nominal 5 percent.
hypotheses.reasoning: Both arms pass with room: recall 1.000 in every replicate of every design, false positives 0.0048 at worst against a nominal 0.05. Held at 0.85 rather than higher because the designs inject up to three chromosomes and thirty replicates, not the two hundred the plan asked for -- a genome with ten abnormal chromosomes was not tested and is not claimed.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A design where recovery falls below 80 percent power, or where unaffected chromosomes are flagged above the nominal rate -- reported as the bound's blind spot for exactly the multi-chromosome case the disease name describes.
hypotheses.statement: The mixing simulation recovers two and three simultaneously affected chromosomes at 10 and 20 percent cell fraction, and does not flag the unaffected ones.

hypotheses.author: step-8
hypotheses.prediction: On simulated meiotic and mitotic trisomies injected at 5, 10 and 20 percent, the five-model comparison assigns the correct mechanism with delta-BIC of 10 or more in fewer than half the replicates; the mechanism is therefore reported as not identifiable rather than called.
hypotheses.reasoning: Supported on its own pre-registered simulation test, and the real-data finding is stronger than the claim it was filed against: the two trisomies are not merely inseparable from each other, no member of the family is usable on this callset. Held at 0.85 rather than higher because the claim names a specific comparison and the real-data evidence is about something broader than it asked.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The comparison separates the two mechanisms at delta-BIC of 10 or more in a majority of replicates -- the mechanism call is then a real measurement and is handed to step 7's Track 2 card.
hypotheses.statement: Mitotic and meiotic trisomy are not separable at delta-BIC of 10 or more from arm-stratified allele-fraction band structure at cell fractions up to 20 percent, at this sample's depth and heterozygous-site counts.

figures.means: The step's headline: fold-over reaches 80% power on all 24 contigs (power rising from 0.18 to 1.00 as fraction rises from 1% to 30% on chr1), while iteration 1's mean-BAF statistic never reaches 80% power on any contig (0.05 to only 0.22 over the same range) — direct evidence that iteration 1's 'every autosome flat' finding used a statistic blind to the exact symmetric-gain signature a mosaic event produces.

figures.means: The second instrument's positive control, read first by design: X reads 0.4873 and Y reads 0.5083 against an expected 0.5 (one copy each in a male proband), confirming the dosage route works before any autosomal claim is trusted. The two denominators track together, meaning no single chromosome is dragging the autosomal median.
figures.name: dosage-per-chromosome.html
figures.reads: Scatter plot, one point per chromosome, of k-mer dosage (sequence contributed, from counting reference-unique 31-mers in the raw reads) measured against two denominators — the autosomal median (with bootstrap error bars) and the total genome-wide k-mer mass — with a shaded band at the one-copy range and X/Y coloured as the control.

figures.means: Same evidence as the interactive scatter: X/Y at ~0.49–0.51 confirms the instrument, and the two denominators' agreement rules out a single chromosome distorting the baseline.
figures.name: dosage-per-chromosome.png
figures.reads: Static version of the same dual-denominator dosage scatter per chromosome.

figures.means: Shows that most of what would look like a dosage 'signal' is actually a GC-content bias: chromosome GC explains 81.7% of the between-chromosome dosage spread (Pearson 0.904) — this correction is what has to be applied before any residual difference can be treated as evidence of an aneuploid cell population, since GC bias is the same order of magnitude as the event being hunted.
figures.name: dosage-composition.html
figures.reads: Scatter of each autosome's measured dosage against its own chromosome-level GC (guanine+cytosine) content fraction, with a fitted trend line.

figures.means: Same evidence as the interactive scatter, establishing the GC correction before any residual is read as a possible aneuploidy signal.
figures.name: dosage-composition.png
figures.reads: Static version of the dosage-vs-chromosome-GC scatter with fitted trend line.

figures.means: After GC correction, the largest residual is chr21 at 2.33 sigma (implied ~1.2% of cells) — not a finding, since with 22 autosomes tested at once roughly one is expected to clear 2 sigma by chance (Bonferroni-corrected p=0.43). The spread of these residuals, not the narrower bootstrap interval, sets the route's honest precision floor at 1.6% of cells (twice the 0.802% residual spread).
figures.name: dosage-residual.html
figures.reads: Bar chart of each chromosome's residual dosage (what is left after removing the GC trend), in units of the residual spread (sigma), with dotted lines at ±2 sigma.

figures.means: Same evidence as the interactive chart: no autosome clears the corrected significance bar after accounting for how many chromosomes were tested at once, so 0 autosomes exceed the corrected null.
figures.name: dosage-residual.png
figures.reads: Static version of the per-chromosome residual-sigma bar chart with the ±2 sigma lines.

figures.means: Shows that no contig exceeds its own, individually-calibrated null — the per-chromosome null construction is what prevents a shallow, low-coverage chromosome from being unfairly flagged just for being noisier, which is the correct comparison for this heterogeneous dataset.
figures.name: bdev-per-chromosome.png
figures.reads: Bar chart of each contig's mean fold-over deviation |BAF−centre|, each compared against a null built from that chromosome's own depth and heterozygous-site count (not a shared threshold), with the null's mean and 95th percentile marked and hemizygous contigs greyed out.

figures.means: Same evidence as the static bars, letting a reader inspect exact deviation values and null bounds per chromosome.
figures.name: bdev-per-chromosome.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the per-chromosome fold-over deviation bars against their individual nulls.

figures.means: Evidence for H055: no chromosome's exclusion shifts the baseline beyond its own bootstrap interval, meaning the denominator every relative dosage/depth statistic on this page divides by is not being propped up or distorted by any single chromosome — the X/Y depth ratio (0.5225/1.5794) is itself the expected male-proband signature and serves as a sanity check that depth measurement works correctly.

figures.reads: Each chromosome's sequencing depth ratio plotted against a leave-one-chromosome-out baseline (the median of per-chromosome medians with each chromosome excluded in turn), with dotted lines marking the measured precision floor of that ratio across autosomes.

figures.means: Same evidence as the static chart, letting a reader confirm the baseline's stability chromosome by chromosome.
figures.name: depth-against-baseline.html

figures.means: Evidence for H057: only a small number of contigs clear ΔBIC≥10, and — as the text alongside establishes — nearly every 'winning' non-normal fit sits at a parameter boundary (the balanced-tract parameter pinned at its 0.900 upper bound), meaning the apparent trisomy leads are model-fitting artefacts rather than genuine mechanism calls; no mechanism is reported for any chromosome as a result.

figures.reads: Interactive version of the per-chromosome model-comparison bars, with hover tooltips for exact BIC values per model.

figures.means: Evidence for H056: every injected chromosome is recovered in every replicate, and untouched chromosomes are falsely flagged at only 0.0048 at worst — far below the nominal 5% — which validates that the genome-wide baseline this whole step's relative statistics divide by remains trustworthy even when 2–3 chromosomes are genuinely abnormal at once (variegated aneuploidy's own defining challenge).

figures.means: Shown beside the mechanism models but deliberately excluded from the likelihood calculation: this statistic is what a monosomy or copy-neutral-loss event would move (by removing heterozygous sites, not shifting their balance), but in a bulk (mixed-cell) sample the diploid cells still generate heterozygous calls, so a drop reflects the variant caller's own detection threshold as much as biology — not a model that can be written down honestly, hence reported as context, not evidence.

hands_to.what: Step 7's Track 2 mechanism card had one row deliberately left open — fact F8, the aneuploidy burden in this specific child's sequenced sample — for this step to measure. Step 8 hands back a null result with a stated limit (no autosome above 2–3% cell fraction, tissue unnamed, X/Y and sub-arm events untestable), which step 7 folded into card version 4 and confirmed via a pre-registered digest test moved no drug-evidence rung, shortlist row, or do-not row.

inherits.what: Step 8 re-derives its own tables from the delivered callset (2,778,844 heterozygous PASS calls) and the raw read store independently of steps 1–7 — it does not depend on the fused diagnosis or any other iteration-2 step's output. It does, however, directly re-test and correct a specific iteration-1 result (entry 037's flat B-allele-fraction karyogram), which is the finding this whole step exists to re-examine with a statistic that actually has power.

narrative.summary: Step 8 re-tests iteration 1's finding that every chromosome looks normal (no mosaic aneuploidy — a chromosome present in the wrong copy number in only some of the cells) in the sequenced sample, and asks the question iteration 1's own statistic could not answer: how small an event could this data even have detected? It found that iteration 1's statistic (the mean B-allele fraction, the average share of reads supporting the non-reference base at heterozygous sites) has essentially no statistical power for exactly the kind of event being hunted — a mosaic gain splits heterozygous sites into two bands symmetric around the middle, so their mean does not move regardless of event size, reaching 80% detection power on 0 of 24 contigs even at a 30% cell fraction. Replacing it with a fold-over deviation statistic (|BAF − centre|, which does move) reaches 80% power on all 24 contigs, giving a genuine detection limit of 2% (chromosomes 1–6) to 3% (chromosomes 7–22) of cells for autosomes, and 5% for X/Y where allele balance is blind by construction. A second, independent k-mer dosage instrument (counting unique 31-letter DNA substrings per chromosome directly in the raw reads, sharing nothing with the allele-balance route past the FASTQ) confirmed one copy each of X and Y (0.4873, 0.5083 against an expected 0.5 — its own positive control) and, after correcting for a chromosome-GC-content bias that explains 81.7% of the between-chromosome variation, found no autosome beyond a corrected precision floor of 1.6% of cells. All seven pre-registered claims were supported. A separate five-model mechanism comparison (normal / monosomy / mitotic trisomy / meiotic trisomy / copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity) fit no usable model on 19 of 22 testable contigs — every apparent trisomy fit hit a parameter boundary, meaning no mechanism can be named for any chromosome.
narrative.verdict: H051 (no chromosome carries a mosaic aneuploidy above its own detection limit) is supported. H052 (the detection limit is ≤10% cell fraction for every autosome) is supported, and by a wider margin than predicted — the actual limit is 2–3%. H053 (fold-over B-deviation detects at a materially lower fraction than iteration 1's statistic) is supported: 24/24 contigs reach 80% power versus 0/24 for the mean-BAF statistic. H054 (the two independent routes — allele balance and k-mer dosage — agree everywhere both can see, and dosage recovers X/Y where allele balance is blind) is supported, by a second instrument sharing nothing with the first past the raw FASTQ reads. H055 (the leave-one-chromosome-out depth baseline is stable) is supported: no single chromosome's exclusion moves it outside its bootstrap interval. H056 (a mixing simulation recovers 2–3 simultaneously-injected abnormal chromosomes without falsely flagging untouched ones) is supported, at a false-flag rate of at most 0.0048 against a nominal 0.05. H057 (mitotic and meiotic trisomy are not separable at ΔBIC≥10) is supported, by an even stronger route than named: the five-model comparison could not fit a usable model at all on 19 of 22 testable contigs because the winning fits sat at a parameter bound, so no mechanism is named for any chromosome.
narrative.why: A negative result ('every chromosome looks flat') is only meaningful if the measurement could have detected the thing it's ruling out; otherwise 'flat' just means 'the instrument was blind,' not 'there is nothing there.' Iteration 1's karyogram used a statistic that is mathematically insensitive to symmetric mosaic gains by construction — without measuring that, the report would have been claiming an absence that its own tool could not have found even at a large event size. This matters directly for step 7's drug-repurposing work: several of Track 2's mechanistic directions (D2, exploiting aneuploid-cell stress) argue from the premise that this child's cells carry a measurable aneuploid burden, and step 7 explicitly left that fact open for this step to measure rather than assume.
